closure_requirements: All modules have a documented shared current trading-day status contract backed by market.trading_calendar.
Paper v2 and Local Data consume the shared status instead of maintaining separate current-day semantics.
No trading-sensitive path silently falls back to weekday-only logic when the calendar provider fails.
The service exposes freshness and coverage diagnostics so operators can distinguish non-trading day from missing/stale calendar data.
Future modules can call the same service/API without duplicating SQL.
BUG-116 implementation removes all weekday fallback behavior from trading-sensitive calendar decisions.
Unified trading-day status API serves normal requests from an automatically maintained filesystem cache derived from market.trading_calendar.
The service warns before calendar coverage expires for the next full month and never requires manual cache generation.
Paper v2 homepage shows current trading-day status, latest ended trading day, and earliest next trading day from the unified API.
Paper v2 runtime, readiness, session, live, replay, and MiniQMT-adjacent paths use the unified calendar provider contract.
description: Expected: AIstock should expose a shared read-only platform trading-day status service backed by market.trading_calendar so Paper v2, Local Data management, simulation runtime, and future live paths read one canonical current-day calendar answer. The service should cache briefly and invalidate after calendar sync, but the database table remains the source of truth. Actual: multiple modules query market.trading_calendar directly or expose module-local helpers; Paper v2 session guard code may fall back to weekday logic on provider errors, and Local Data owns calendar sync UX without publishing a shared status contract. Supplement 2026-05-24: all weekday fallback logic must be removed. The official service must build and maintain an AIstock-owned filesystem cache from market.trading_calendar so normal API reads do not query PostgreSQL on every request. Cache rebuild/refresh must be automatic, monthly-aware, and warn when DB calendar rows do not cover the next full calendar month. Paper v2 overview must display current trading-day status, latest ended trading day, and earliest next trading day from the unified API.

events.note: User asked whether Paper v2, Local Data, and future modules should share a global current trading-day status based on the synced annual trading calendar.
Created GitHub issue #187 and mirrored BUG-116 JSON.
User required removal of all weekday fallback logic, automatic filesystem cache backed by market.trading_calendar, monthly coverage warning, and Paper v2 overview trading-day status display.

Audit keeps BUG-116 open: backend TradingCalendarStatusService/API and Paper v2 overview status exist and live /api/v1/trading-calendar/status returns 200, but Local Data status display plus /api/calendar/sync cache refresh/invalidation and full freshness/timezone semantics are not fully proven.

non_goals: Do not replace market.trading_calendar as the source of truth.
Do not add a manually editable AIstock global trading-day flag.
Do not change QE/backtest historical calendar semantics.
Do not start or restart production 8001/3000 as part of issue registration.
Do not keep any weekday fallback as a compatibility mode for trading-sensitive paths.
Do not require operators to manually generate or refresh the filesystem cache.
Do not make the filesystem cache a new source of truth; it is a derived cache from market.trading_calendar.
required_verification: A shared platform calendar status service/API returns today, is_trading_day, latest_trading_day_lte_today, previous_trading_day, next_trading_day, source, coverage, and freshness/audit status from market.trading_calendar.
The service uses a bounded per-process cache or request cache with explicit invalidation after successful /calendar/sync; it does not create a manually edited global flag.
Paper v2 same-day/session/readiness/day-run paths use the shared provider contract or injected adapter and do not fall back to weekday-only logic for trading-sensitive decisions.
Local Data management displays the same platform status and refreshes it after trade calendar sync.
Missing or stale calendar coverage fails fast with calendar_missing/calendar_stale status instead of silently claiming trading or non-trading day.
Tests cover normal trading day, weekend/holiday, make-up trading day, missing calendar rows, stale future coverage, cache invalidation after sync, and Paper v2 no-weekday-fallback behavior.

Validation record includes DESIGN-COMPLIANCE-001 item-by-item matrix and reports production_ddl_gate, production_frontend_dependency_gate, production_backend_dependency_gate, and whether production 8001/3000 were touched.
All weekday fallback logic is removed from Paper v2 and platform trading-sensitive paths; tests or static checks prove calendar decisions do not use weekday() or browser/local weekday as fallback.
The official trading-day status service builds an AIstock-owned filesystem cache from market.trading_calendar and normal API access reads the cache instead of querying PostgreSQL on every request.
Cache rebuild/update is automatic when the cache is missing, stale, crossed a calendar-month boundary, or /api/calendar/sync succeeds; no manual cache-generation step is required.
The cache records coverage_start, coverage_end, generated_at, source_row_count, source_checksum or equivalent provenance, and cache_status/warnings.
If database rows do not cover every calendar date through the next full calendar month, the service returns a warning that tells operators to refresh market.trading_calendar in time.
Current date freshness checks require an explicit current Asia/Shanghai date row in the cached calendar; missing current-date row fails fast as calendar_missing_current_date.

Paper v2 overview page (/paper-v2) displays whether the current date is a trading day, the latest ended trading day, and the earliest next trading day from the unified API, including cache warning state.
API tests instrument or fake the repository to prove repeated status calls use filesystem cache and do not hit the database every time.
Paper v2 timezone-sensitive defaults use Asia/Shanghai business date from the unified service, not dt.date.today(), datetime.now() naive, or frontend UTC ISO slicing.
